Chronicle

What's new
  • Auto-delivery for connected recipients — when you share with someone whose email is in your Connections, Chronicle delivers the memory directly to their inbox — no link to copy and send. See Sharing Memories.
  • Guest contribution links — generate a permanent link that lets anyone submit memories and documents directly into your Chronicle inbox. Perfect for collaborative research. See Contribution Links.
  • Accept all — in the Sharing inbox, accept an entire batch of incoming memories with one click rather than one at a time.
User Manual
by Remembory

A personal life journal for your whole story.

Chronicle is a personal life journal that lives entirely on your computer as a single HTML file. Open it in any web browser and your memories are stored locally — nothing leaves your device unless you choose to share.

This manual covers every feature in Chronicle. Whether you are just getting started or looking to make the most of a specific capability, you will find step-by-step instructions throughout.

Getting Started

  1. Visit Chronicle on Remembory in your browser
  2. Chronicle opens and you are ready to record your first memory
  3. Bookmark the page for quick access — your memories will always be there when you return
Chronicle works offline after your first visit. A service worker caches everything so you can use it anywhere, even without an internet connection. Updates happen silently in the background — you always have the latest version without doing anything.
Your memories are stored in your browser on your device — they never leave it. If you use multiple browsers (e.g. Chrome and Safari), your memories will be separate in each. Pick one browser and stick to it, or use the backup feature to keep them in sync.

Your Name & Email

Before sharing memories with others, set your name and email address so recipients know who sent them.

  1. Click the ⚙ Settings button in the top right corner
  2. Enter your name in the Your name & email field
  3. Enter your email address below your name
  4. Settings are saved automatically as you type
Your email is only used when you share memories. It is stored locally and never sent anywhere automatically.

Navigating Chronicle

Chronicle has several views, each offering a different way to see and interact with your memories.

On desktop, navigation buttons appear in the top right of the header. On mobile, a tab bar appears at the bottom of the screen with icon buttons for each view.

ViewWhat it does
◉ LifeYour home view — memories as a grid of decade cards showing activity across your whole life
≡ ListA scrollable chronological list of all memories with search and tag filtering
☰ IndexBrowse memories by tag, person, organisation, or location
🗺 MapA world map showing where memories took place, with clickable pins
🖨 PrintGenerate a formatted document of your life story to print or save as PDF
↑ ImportBring in new memories from photos or email files

The Header

The header stays fixed at the top as you scroll. It contains:

  • Chronicle title — click it to return to the Life view from anywhere
  • Breadcrumb trail — shows where you are, e.g. 1980s › 1987 › The summer holiday
  • ← Back button — appears when navigating inside a decade or memory
  • + Add button — opens the form to record a new memory
  • ⚙ Settings button — opens the settings drawer

The Life View

The Life view is your starting point — your whole life at a glance, organised by decade.

Decade Cards

Each decade card shows:

  • The decade label (e.g. 1980s)
  • A mini bar chart showing memory count for each year in that decade
  • Coloured dots representing the most common tags in that decade
  • The specific years that contain memories

Click any decade card to open the Decade View.

Decade View

Shows all ten years within a decade as a vertical timeline. Years with memories show a preview title and count. Empty years appear dimmed. Click a year to open the Year View, or click a coloured memory dot to go directly to that memory.

Year View

Shows all memories within a year, grouped by month or season along a vertical timeline. Memories are grouped as follows:

  • Day-precise or month-precise memories are placed in their correct month
  • Season memories are placed at the start (Early), middle (Mid), or end (Late) of the year
  • Year-only memories are grouped together at the top
Adding even a few memories to each year creates a rich, satisfying picture of that time when you look back at the Year View.

The List View

The List view shows all memories in a single scrollable chronological timeline, grouped into decades. This is the best view for searching across your whole archive.

Searching

A search box appears at the top. Type any word or phrase to filter memories in real time — Chronicle searches across both titles and content.

Filtering by Tag

A tag dropdown sits next to the search box. Select any tag to show only memories with that tag. You can combine tag filtering with a text search simultaneously.

Adding a Memory

Click the + Add button in the header to open the memory form. Only the title is required — fill in everything else at whatever level of detail feels right.

Title

Give the memory a name that will mean something to you later. The title appears in all views and is the primary way you will find the memory again.

Date — Fuzzy Dating

Chronicle understands that not every memory has a precise date. You can record dates at six levels of precision:

PrecisionWhen to use itExample
ExactYou know the specific date14 March 1985
MonthYou remember the year and monthMarch 1985
Part of yearYou remember roughly when in the year — Early, Mid, or LateEarly 1985
YearYou remember the year but not much else1985
DecadeYou only know the rough era1980s
UncertainYou have a best guess but no evidence1985?

Use the date type selector to choose your precision level, then fill in the fields that appear.

Memories marked as uncertain display with a ? suffix so you can tell at a glance which dates need verification.

Don't let uncertainty stop you from recording a memory. A memory with just a year is infinitely better than no memory at all.

Visibility

Each memory has a visibility setting that controls whether it can appear on your public profile (a subscriber feature). The default is Private, which means the memory stays on your device and is never published.

SettingWho can see it
PrivateOnly you, on this device. Never published. This is the default.
PublicAnyone who visits your profile page
SubscribersVisitors who have a valid Remembory subscription key
ConnectedPeople who have received a shared memory from you
PresentOnly people tagged in this specific memory who have a profile

Visibility only matters if you publish a public profile from Settings. If you haven't done that, all memories remain private regardless of this setting.

The visibility field appears at the bottom of the add and edit memory forms.

Location

Enter the primary location where the memory took place. As you type, Chronicle suggests locations you have used before. This location appears in the memory card subtitle and on the Map view.

Additional Locations

For memories that span multiple places — a road trip, a multi-city holiday, a house move — add extra locations using the Additional Locations field. Type a location and press Enter or click + Add. Each location will appear on the Map view.

Tags

Tags help you categorise and find memories later. Chronicle includes 12 preset tags:

TagSuggested use
ChildhoodEarly life memories
FamilyMemories involving family
TravelTrips, journeys, and adventures away from home
EducationSchool, university, courses, and learning
EmploymentCareer, jobs, and professional life
LoveRelationships and romance
HealthMedical events, illness, recovery, fitness milestones
MilestoneSignificant life events and achievements
HomeHouses, moves, and domestic life
FriendshipFriends and social connections
AdventureChallenges, risks, and new experiences
LossBereavement, endings, and grief

You can also create custom tags. Type a tag name in the custom field and press Add. Remove custom tags from the picker when no longer needed.

People & Organisations

People — add the names of people who were part of this memory. As you type, Chronicle suggests names from your existing records. Each person tagged will appear in the People index.

To add: type a name and press Enter or click + Add. To remove: click the × next to their name.

Organisations — add any organisations relevant to the memory: schools, companies, clubs, hospitals. These are indexed separately from people.

Photos & Media

Click the + button in the media area to attach photos to a memory. Multiple photos can be attached. They appear in the detail view, and a thumbnail shows on the memory card in timeline views.

When importing photos via the Import feature, EXIF date data is read automatically, placing photos on your timeline without any manual date entry.

Saving

Click Save to Chronicle to save the memory. It immediately appears in all relevant views. A small ✓ confirmation tick appears briefly in the header.

The Memory Detail View

Click any memory card to open its full detail view. This shows:

  • The date, location, and dominant author (if applicable) in the subtitle
  • The memory title as a large heading
  • Tag chips, people badges, and organisation badges
  • Any attached photos
  • The full memory text
  • Perspectives from other people (if any have been added or shared)
  • Edit, Delete, and Share buttons
  • The Historical Context section at the bottom

Editing a Memory

In the detail view, click Edit to reopen the memory form with all fields populated. Make your changes and click Save Changes.

Deleting a Memory

In the detail view, click Delete. You will be asked to confirm before the memory is permanently removed.

Deletion is permanent. If you are unsure, consider exporting a backup first before deleting.

The Index View

The Index view lets you browse memories by category rather than by time. Access it from the navigation — it has four tabs.

Tags Tab

Shows all tags used across your memories, with a count of how many memories carry each tag. Click any tag to see all matching memories displayed as cards.

People Tab

Shows everyone in your index with a count of memories. People with no memories yet are sorted to the top. Use the filter chips to narrow by relationship, linked organisation, or linked location. Click + add person to record someone before writing any memories about them.

Organisations Tab

The same as the People tab, but for organisations. Use + add org to record an organisation independently.

Locations Tab

Shows all locations in your index. Locations without coordinates show a ⚠️ indicator — they won't appear on the map until coordinates are set. Click ⚠ Set coords to enter them manually. Use + add location to record a place before writing any memories about it.

Relationships Tab

Groups people by their relationship type — family, friend, colleague, and so on. Click any relationship to see all the people in it.

Groups Tab

Shows named groups of people. See Groups below for full details.

People & Organisations Manager

Access from Index → People tab → Manage, or via the ⚙ Settings drawer.

Renaming

Click Rename next to any name, type the corrected name, and press Enter. All memories, linked organisations, locations, and group memberships update automatically.

Linking Organisations & Locations

Under each person's entry, click + link org or + link location to associate them with organisations or places. Multiple connections per person are supported. These appear as filter chips in the People index.

Adding Email Addresses

Enter an email under a person's entry in the People tab. This lets Chronicle verify that incoming shared memories are from someone you know.

Deleting

Click Remove to remove a person or organisation from the index. This does not delete the memories they appear in.

Groups

Groups let you organise people into named collections — Family, School friends, Work colleagues, and so on. Clicking a group in the memory form adds all its members at once.

Creating a Group

  1. Go to Index → Groups tab
  2. Click + new group
  3. Type a name and press Enter or click Create

Adding Members

Click + add member inside a group row and start typing. Only people already in your index appear as suggestions.

Using a Group in a Memory

When adding or editing a memory, group pill buttons appear above the People field. Clicking one adds all its members instantly — useful for recurring gatherings, family events, or group trips.

Renaming & Deleting

Click Rename to rename a group. Click Delete to remove it — members are unaffected.

The Map View

The Map view plots all your memories on an interactive world map, powered by OpenStreetMap. Every location in your memories — primary and additional — gets a coloured pin.

Using the Map

  • Zoom in and out using the + / − buttons or your scroll wheel
  • Click and drag to pan
  • Click any pin to see a popup with the memory title, date, and a button to open the full memory

Locations are geocoded (converted to map coordinates) the first time they appear. Chronicle caches these results locally so the map loads quickly on subsequent visits.

Map Language

The map shows English place names by default. Click Switch to local names in the map legend to toggle to local-language tiles.

Coordinates

When Chronicle geocodes a location, it saves the coordinates to your Locations index so subsequent map loads are instant. To correct a misplaced location:

  1. Go to Index → Locations tab
  2. Click ⚠ Set coords next to the location
  3. Enter coordinates as lat, lng — e.g. -33.8688, 151.2093
  4. Click Save

Manually set coordinates show a ✏ symbol and are never overridden by automatic geocoding.

Use consistent, specific location names — "Melbourne, Australia" rather than just "Melbourne" helps the geocoder find the right place, especially for common city names.
Geocoding requires an internet connection the first time a new location is resolved. Once cached, the map works fully offline.

Importing Memories

The Import view lets you bring in memories from photos or emails, saving you from entering all the details by hand.

Importing from Photos

Chronicle reads EXIF date data embedded in JPEG photos, automatically placing them on your timeline.

  1. Click Import in the navigation
  2. Select the Photos tab
  3. Drag photos onto the drop zone, or click it to browse your files
  4. Chronicle displays each photo with its extracted date and fields for title, location, and tags
  5. Review and edit the details for each photo
  6. Use the Include / Skip button to deselect any photos you don't want
  7. Click Save to create the memories
You can import many photos at once. Chronicle processes them all and lets you review each before saving.
If a photo has no EXIF date (common with scanned prints or screenshots), a warning will show and you can enter the date manually.

Cloud Sync

Subscribers can sync their Chronicle across devices using cloud sync. Your data is encrypted on your device before upload — we cannot read it.

  1. Go to Settings → Backup & Restore
  2. Under Cloud Sync, enter a sync passphrase (used to encrypt your data)
  3. Click Push to cloud to upload your Chronicle
  4. On another device, enter the same licence key and passphrase, then click Pull from cloud

If a memory has been edited on both devices, Chronicle shows a conflict resolution dialog where you can choose to keep your local version, use the cloud version, or merge both together.

Photos are synced separately and encrypted with the same passphrase. A progress bar shows upload and download progress.

Your sync passphrase is not the same as your Chronicle lock password. If you forget it, your cloud data cannot be recovered.

Sharing Memories

Chronicle lets you share memories with the people who were part of them. Shared memories open automatically in the recipient's Chronicle — no app needed, no import steps.

Sending shared memories requires a subscription. The ✉ Share button is visible on all memories but greyed out for free users — hovering shows a tooltip. Receiving shared memories is free for everyone.

Enter your licence key in ⚙ Settings → Subscription to unlock sharing. See Subscription for how to get one.

How Sharing Works

Sharing in Chronicle is link-based. When you share a memory, a private short link is created. The recipient clicks the link, sees a preview, and the memory imports automatically into their Chronicle. The link is single-use — it stops working once collected.

A personal note is required to share — at least one sentence explaining why you are sharing. This keeps sharing thoughtful rather than mechanical.

Sharing a Memory

  1. Open a memory and click Share
  2. Select who you are sharing with — only people tagged in the current memory are shown
  3. Choose which memories to include — the current memory is pre-selected, but you can add others from the checklist
  4. Enter your name (pre-filled from Settings, editable) — this will be tagged in the memory on the recipient's side
  5. Write a personal note (at least one sentence is required)
  6. Click Get shareable link — a short private link is generated
  7. Copy the link and send it by any means — text message, email, messaging app
The link expires after 30 days and is deleted once the recipient collects it. Your memories never leave your device permanently — the shared payload is a temporary copy.

Auto-delivery for Connected Recipients

If a recipient has an email address in your People registry or Connections, Chronicle can deliver the memory directly to their Chronicle inbox — without you needing to copy and send a link manually.

When you click Get shareable link and some recipients have known email addresses, the share panel displays the delivery mode for each:

  • → inbox — the memory will be delivered directly. Nothing to copy or send — just click the button.
  • Copy link — the recipient doesn't have a known email, so you copy the link and send it yourself.

To add an email address to someone in your People index:

  1. Go to Index → People tab
  2. Find the person and expand their entry
  3. Enter their email address in the email field

Alternatively, when adding a connection in ⚙ Settings → Connections, you can include their email address at that point.

Setting up email addresses for family members once means sharing with them in future requires zero extra steps — just click Share and the delivery happens automatically.

Receiving a Shared Memory

  1. Click the share link — it opens a bridge page showing who shared and how many memories
  2. If you opened the link inside a messaging app, the page will prompt you to open it in Safari or Chrome — tap the menu icon and choose Open in browser
  3. Once in your real browser, click Open in Chronicle
  4. Chronicle loads and shows an import prompt — click Save to my Chronicle
Share links expire after 30 days and are deleted once collected. No subscription is needed to receive memories.

Known vs unknown senders

Chronicle checks whether the sender's email address matches someone already in your People registry:

  • Known sender — the dialog appears normally with a warm "Save to my Chronicle" button
  • Unknown sender — an amber warning appears noting the sender is not in your contacts. The accept button is more subdued and labelled "Accept anyway". This gives you pause to consider whether you know who sent the file before accepting.

Accepting multiple memories at once

When a delivery contains more than one memory, each appears individually with its own Accept button. You can also click ✓ Accept all to save every memory in the delivery at once — useful when someone has shared a whole batch of family memories.

Contribution Links

A contribution link is a permanent invite link you can share with anyone — a researcher, a family member, a historical society — inviting them to submit memories, documents, or information directly into your Chronicle inbox. Unlike a share link, a contribution link doesn't expire and can be used multiple times.

The person who receives the link doesn't need a Chronicle account. They fill in a simple form with their name, a subject, and their contribution. When they submit, it arrives in your Sharing → Contributions inbox where you can review and accept each submission individually.

Creating a Contribution Link

  1. Click the ✉ Share button in the navigation (or on any memory)
  2. Select the Contribution Links tab
  3. Add an optional note to display on the contribution form (e.g. what kind of information you are looking for)
  4. Click Create contribution link
  5. Copy the link and send it to whoever you want to invite
Share your contribution link with family members or friends and let them add what they know directly to your Chronicle inbox without needing to set up Chronicle themselves.

Reviewing Contributions

  1. Go to Share → Contributions tab (or look for the badge on the Share button)
  2. Review each submission — you can see the contributor's name, their content, and any attached notes
  3. Click Accept to add it to your Chronicle, or dismiss to ignore it
Contributions are not automatically added to your Chronicle — you review and accept each one. You stay in full control of what enters your records.

Revoking a Link

In the Contribution Links tab, click Revoke next to any link to deactivate it. Anyone who visits the link after revocation will see an expired-link page.

Perspectives

When a memory is shared with you, the sender's original version becomes a perspective — their account of the event, preserved alongside yours.

Perspectives appear in the memory detail view beneath the main content, in a dedicated Perspectives panel. Each perspective shows the author's name, their text, and when it was added.

Adding Your Own Perspective

Once a memory has been shared with you, you can add your own version of events:

  1. Open the shared memory
  2. Scroll to the Perspectives panel
  3. Click Add my perspective
  4. Write your version of the memory
  5. Choose whether your version should be the main timeline entry (see Dominant Perspective below)
  6. Click Save perspective

Sharing Back

Once you have added your perspective, a Share back option appears at the bottom of the Perspectives panel. This lets you send your version back to the original sender, so they can read your account and add it to their own Chronicle.

Dominant Perspective

By default, when a memory is shared with you, the main timeline entry shows no content (since it is the sender's memory, not yours). You can choose which version appears in timeline views using the dominant perspective feature.

When adding your perspective, you will see two radio options:

  • My version — use your account as the main entry shown in timelines
  • Their version — keep the sender's original as the main timeline entry

You can also change this later from within the Perspectives panel:

  • Click make dominant on a perspective to promote it to the main timeline entry
  • Click remove from timeline to revert the current dominant back to the panel
When a perspective is set as dominant, the author's name appears in the memory card subtitle in timeline views — e.g. 1987 · Melbourne · John's memory — so you always know whose account you are reading.

Print & Export

Chronicle can generate a formatted document of your life story — suitable for printing, saving as PDF, or sharing with family as a document.

Click 🖨 Print in the navigation to open the Print view.

Scope

Choose how much of your Chronicle to include:

OptionWhat it includes
All memoriesYour entire Chronicle from the earliest memory to the most recent
One decadeA single decade — select from the dropdown
One yearA single year — select the decade first, then the year

Content Level

OptionWhat it shows
Full memoriesComplete text, photos, people, and perspectives for every memory
Headings onlyDate and title for each memory — a scannable timeline without content
Table of contentsA compact tabular list with people listed per entry, organised by decade

Additional Options

  • Photos — include or exclude attached photos (Full memories mode only)
  • People & orgs — show people and organisation badges, and include a People index at the end
  • Tags — show tag labels on each memory

Printing

Click 🖨 Print / Save as PDF to open your browser's print dialog. To save as a PDF instead of printing, select Save as PDF (or Microsoft Print to PDF on Windows) as the destination.

The print options panel automatically hides when you print — only the formatted story goes to the printer or PDF.

People Index

When People & orgs is enabled and you are printing Full memories or Headings, a People Index is automatically generated at the end of the document. It lists every person alphabetically, with the title and year of each memory they appear in — like a book index.

Subscription

Chronicle is free to use as a personal journal. A subscription ($20/year) unlocks sending shared memories and Genealogy mode.

What's Free

  • Complete life timeline journal, photos, places, tags
  • People groups, location & organisation linking, filter chips
  • Map view with coordinates and language toggle
  • Print & export
  • Receiving shared memories from others
  • Works entirely offline — no account ever required

What Requires a Subscription

  • Sending shared memories to others
  • Guest contribution links
Subscribe at remembory.net — $20 AUD/year via card or PayPal.

Backup & Restore

Chronicle stores your memories in your browser on your device — they never leave it. This is great for privacy, but it means you are responsible for keeping a copy. Clearing your browser's history, cache, or site data will permanently erase your memories with no way to recover them.

Back up regularly. Treat your Chronicle backup the way you would treat irreplaceable photos. Download a backup at least once a month and keep it somewhere safe — a cloud drive, an external disk, or email it to yourself. The file contains everything: memories, photos, and settings.

Downloading a Backup

  1. Click ⚙ Settings in the top navigation
  2. In the Backup section, click 💾 Download backup
  3. Save the file somewhere safe — a cloud drive, external disk, or email it to yourself as an attachment
The easiest habit: after adding a batch of memories, email the backup file to yourself. It stays in your sent mail forever as an offsite copy.

Restoring from a Backup

  1. Click ⚙ Settings
  2. Click ⬆ Restore from file
  3. Select your previously downloaded backup file
  4. Your memories will be restored — existing memories are merged with the backup, not overwritten
For a clean restore with no merging, go to Settings → Reset → Clear all memories first, then restore from your backup file.

Clearing All Memories

To erase everything and start fresh, go to ⚙ Settings → Reset and click 🗑 Clear all memories. You will be asked to confirm. Download a backup first if you want to keep your data.

Privacy

Chronicle is built on a single principle: your memories belong to you.

  • No account required — Chronicle needs no login or registration
  • No cloud storage — all data is stored in your browser's local storage on your own device
  • No tracking or analytics — Chronicle does not send any data anywhere by default
  • No subscription — Chronicle is free forever
  • Sharing is always opt-in — nothing is shared unless you explicitly initiate it

The only time data leaves your device is when you:

  • Share a memory by email (you control what is attached and sent)
  • Generate a share link (the memory is uploaded to your own Cloudflare Worker)
  • Use Historical Context (the memory date and location are sent to the Anthropic API using your own key)
  • View the Map (location names are sent to a geocoding service to resolve coordinates)
Map geocoding results are cached locally after the first lookup — so each location is only ever sent to the geocoding service once.
